evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline ASR/RSR gains are corroborated on held-out tasks across three selective memory systems, multiple LLM backbones, eight target retrievers, and a real-world Hermes Agent deployment, none of which were used to optimize the trigger.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end ISR, RSR@1, ASR, and ACC measured on held-out queries across A-Mem, LangMem, Mem0, multiple LLM backbones, eight target embedding models, and the Hermes Agent.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Surrogate BERT-base NER classification loss plus MiniLM embedding concentration and isolation losses used to optimize the trigger.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported metrics (ISR, RSR@1, ASR, ACC) clearly corroborate the claims that MemPoison achieves high attack success (ASR up to 0.95) and preserves benign accuracy under realistic selective memory conditions where prior methods fail [E5a9e40183344219e-B0003, E5a9e40183344219e-B0045, E5a9e40183344219e-B0046, E5a9e40183344219e-B0073, E5a9e40183344219e-B0075].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is extensive and well-controlled across three application domains (personal, medical, financial), three modern selective memory mechanisms (A-Mem, LangMem, Mem0), and multiple LLM backbones [E5a9e40183344219e-B0041, E5a9e40183344219e-B0042, E5a9e40183344219e-B0045, E5a9e40183344219e-B0046]. It incorporates rigorous baselines, ablations, cross-embedder transfer experiments, lifecycle simulations, real-world case studies on Hermes Agent, and mechanistic analyses linking vulnerability to embedding anisotropy [E5a9e40183344219e-B0052, E5a9e40183344219e-B0065, E5a9e40183344219e-B0077, E5a9e40183344219e-B0088].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance was corroborated on held-out tasks across disparate production backbones (e.g., GPT-5.4, Qwen3-max), diverse memory architectures (Mem0, LangMem, A-Mem), 8 different retrieval encoders, and the real-world Hermes Agent [E5a9e40183344219e-B0045, E5a9e40183344219e-B0062, E5a9e40183344219e-B0065, E5a9e40183344219e-B0077].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end task metrics (ASR, ISR, RSR@1, and ACC) measured across independent LLM agent pipelines, different selective memory frameworks, and distinct target embedding models [E5a9e40183344219e-B0042, E5a9e40183344219e-B0048, E5a9e40183344219e-B0062, E5a9e40183344219e-B0065].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Surrogate BERT-base NER classification loss and surrogate dense embedding geometry (MiniLM concentration and isolation losses) [E5a9e40183344219e-B0033, E5a9e40183344219e-B0034, E5a9e40183344219e-B0035, E5a9e40183344219e-B0036].

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss key limitations, including performance degradation against strongly aligned front-end models that filter malicious inputs during extraction (such as Claude-Opus-4.6 in deployment), lower cross-embedder transferability to specific architectures like aMPNet, and the scope being bounded to dense retrieval rather than hybrid BM25 schemes [E5a9e40183344219e-B0077, E5a9e40183344219e-B0078, E5a9e40183344219e-B0090].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formalizing multi-objective losses for entity masquerading via surrogate NER and discrete HotFlip-style coordinate search, as well as embedding concentration and isolation objectives over dense representation spaces [E5a9e40183344219e-B0032, E5a9e40183344219e-B0033, E5a9e40183344219e-B0034, E5a9e40183344219e-B0036]. The paper specifies concrete algorithms and operational phases under clear threat model constraints [E5a9e40183344219e-B0022, E5a9e40183344219e-B0036].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped security study addressing an important vulnerability in modern selective agent memory architectures. The methodology, experimental controls, comprehensive ablations, defense tests, and mechanistic explanations provide robust evidence satisfying all scientific criteria.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces MemPoison, an optimization-based backdoor memory poisoning framework for LLM agents designed to bypass selective memory extraction and rewriting pipelines using semantic relational bridging, entity masquerading, and joint embedding optimization [E5a9e40183344219e-B0002, E5a9e40183344219e-B0011, E5a9e40183344219e-B0012].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped security study addressing an important vulnerability in modern selective agent memory architectures. The methodology, experimental controls, comprehensive ablations, defense tests, and mechanistic explanations provide robust evidence satisfying all scientific criteria.
